items.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Phil was my mentor because I met him when I was with Jimmie Lunceford.

ctx.x: Okay, let’s go back – um go forward now to when you decided you wanted to study more. What did you do? How did you turn down these recording contracts, all these gigs? So what did you do?
Alright I’m here now, back into um, back into Los Angeles. I have a mentor I call – one of my mentors is a man I’m going to bring up. I don’t know if you know his name was Phil Moore.

items.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

ctx.x: Now didn’t you work with some other singer later on? Some guy that used to be a waiter?

Yeah, that happened with my band of course. We were, and Snooky was with me at the time. We were together, you know, Snooky and I we played with Les Hite’s band here in Los Angeles. We played with Phil Moore. We made records with everybody. We played for Warner Brothers and MGM.
And for movies. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
